body.claim: settle ≠ consent / purpose / agent authority — Circle Facilitator Service settles EIP-3009 USDC authorizations; it does not verify transaction purpose or confirm agent authority scope.

evidence.quote: Facilitator Service verifies buyer-signed EIP-3009 USDC payment authorizations under the x402 protocol only — it does not hold, control, or transmit user funds, verify transaction purpose, or confirm agent authority scope. On Base and Polygon, settlements are subject to blockchain reorganization risk; Circle does not guarantee fund receipt. Arc settlements are final.

Circle just made Arc a real x402 rail, not a future roadmap item. Arc mainnet is live, and Circle’s hosted x402 facilitator now settles USDC across Arc, Base and Polygon. One detail matters: Circle says the facilitator doesn’t verify transaction purpose or agent authority scope. So settlement is getting easier. The independent “should this buyer sign this exact deal?” check is still a separate job.

settlement.note: USDC moved on Arc: Circle Facilitator Service verified the buyer's EIP-3009 signature and settled it. Nothing in this flow checked why the buyer paid or whether the signing agent was authorized to. Settlement ≠ consent.
